nodes.description: Private mapping(bytes32 => uint256) in TimelockController storing the ready timestamp of each scheduled operation id; written by _schedule, _afterCall and cancel.
Private uint256 minimum delay required before any scheduled operation becomes executable; set in the TimelockController constructor and changed only via updateDelay.
Private mapping(bytes32 => RoleData) in AccessControl holding role membership and each role's admin role; the backing storage of all authorization checks.
Internal constant uint256(1) sentinel written into _timestamps to mark an operation as already executed.
Timelock constructor: revokes TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE from the deployer (_msgSender) and grants it to the supplied admin address, fixing the delay at 6545 seconds.
TimelockController constructor: sets role admins, grants TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE to deployer and to the contract itself, registers proposers/executors and initializes _minDelay.
Schedules a single operation; restricted by onlyRole(PROPOSER_ROLE), computes the operation id and stores timestamp = block.timestamp + delay via _schedule.
Schedules a batch of operations; PROPOSER_ROLE gated, validates array lengths and stores a single ready timestamp for the batch id.
Private helper: rejects already scheduled ids, enforces delay >= getMinDelay() and writes block.timestamp + delay into _timestamps.
PROPOSER_ROLE gated cancellation of a pending operation; deletes the entry in _timestamps.
Payable single-operation execution gated by onlyRoleOrOpenRole(EXECUTOR_ROLE); hashes parameters, checks readiness and performs an external call.
Payable batch execution gated by onlyRoleOrOpenRole(EXECUTOR_ROLE); loops over arrays and performs one external call per element.
Private pre-execution check: requires isOperationReady(id) and that the predecessor is zero or already done.
Private post-execution bookkeeping: re-checks readiness and marks the operation done by writing _DONE_TIMESTAMP into _timestamps.
Private function performing the low-level target.call{value:value}(data) with an arbitrary caller-supplied target and calldata, then emits CallExecuted.
External self-only function changing the minimum timelock delay; requires msg.sender == address(this) so it must be reached through the timelock itself.
Grants a role; protected by onlyRole(getRoleAdmin(role)) and delegates to _grantRole.
Revokes a role; protected by onlyRole(getRoleAdmin(role)) and delegates to _revokeRole.
Allows an account to give up its own role; requires account == _msgSender() then delegates to _revokeRole.
Internal unchecked role grant mutating _roles and emitting RoleGranted.
Internal unchecked role revocation mutating _roles and emitting RoleRevoked.
Internal bootstrap role assignment without any caller check; only meant for constructors.
Internal function changing which admin role controls a given role; writes _roles[role].adminRole.
Public view returning _roles[role].members[account]; the primitive authorization predicate.
Internal revert-if-missing check used by the onlyRole/onlyRoleOrOpenRole modifiers.
Pure function computing the operation id as keccak256(abi.encode(target, value, data, predecessor, salt)).
Pure function computing the batch operation id from targets, values, datas, predecessor and salt.
View returning true when the stored timestamp is greater than _DONE_TIMESTAMP and not later than block.timestamp.
View returning the scheduled timestamp for an operation id from _timestamps.
View returning the current minimum delay from _minDelay.
Context helper returning msg.sender; the indirection point through which the caller identity flows into AccessControl and Timelock.

Low-level arbitrary target.call{value: value}(data) with attacker-influenced target, value and calldata; executes before TimelockController state finalization (_afterCall), creating a reentrancy surface.
Caller-controlled address used for role checks, admin bootstrap and the updateDelay self-call guard.
Miner-influenceable timestamp used to compute when a scheduled operation becomes ready.
target address parameter of execute; becomes the destination of the low-level call.
value amount parameter of execute; forwarded as the ETH value of the low-level call.
Calldata bytes parameter of execute; forwarded verbatim to the external call.
delay parameter of schedule/scheduleBatch used to compute the readiness timestamp.
newDelay parameter of updateDelay that will replace the stored _minDelay.
admin address parameter of the Timelock constructor that receives TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE.
bytes32 role identifier used throughout AccessControl (grantRole, revokeRole, _checkRole, _setRoleAdmin).
address account parameter of grantRole/revokeRole/renounceRole whose membership is modified.
minDelay parameter of the TimelockController constructor stored into _minDelay.
Local bytes32 id computed via hashOperation/hashOperationBatch inside schedule, execute and their batch variants.
Loop counter i used when iterating over targets/values/datas arrays in constructors and batch functions.
Local timestamp read from getTimestamp inside isOperationReady and compared with block.timestamp.

edges.reason: msg.sender is returned by the Context._msgSender helper and thus flows into every role check in the timelock.
The Timelock constructor uses _msgSender() to revoke the deployer's TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE, a privileged bootstrap authorization decision.
The caller identity obtained from _msgSender() is passed to _checkRole by the onlyRole/onlyRoleOrOpenRole modifiers.
renounceRole compares the account argument against _msgSender() to prevent revoking roles of other accounts.
_grantRole emits RoleGranted with _msgSender() as the sender of the grant.
_revokeRole emits RoleRevoked with _msgSender() as the sender of the revocation.
updateDelay gates the delay change on msg.sender == address(this); an incorrect guard would let anyone change the timelock delay.
onlyRoleOrOpenRole consults hasRole(role, address(0)) and falls back to checking the raw caller's role.
_schedule writes block.timestamp + delay, making operation readiness dependent on the miner-influenceable block timestamp.
isOperationReady compares the stored timestamp with block.timestamp, so executability depends on the block timestamp.
_schedule stores the computed readiness timestamp into the _timestamps mapping.
_schedule requires delay >= getMinDelay(), reading the configured minimum delay.
_schedule rejects ids that already exist by consulting getTimestamp through isOperation.
_afterCall marks the operation done by writing _DONE_TIMESTAMP into _timestamps.
cancel deletes the operation's entry from the _timestamps mapping.
schedule delegates the timestamp bookkeeping to the private _schedule helper.
scheduleBatch delegates the timestamp bookkeeping to the private _schedule helper.
schedule derives the operation id by calling hashOperation.
scheduleBatch derives the batch operation id by calling hashOperationBatch.
execute recomputes the operation id with hashOperation from the supplied parameters.
execute runs the _beforeCall readiness and predecessor checks before invoking the target.
execute performs the single external call through the private _call helper.
execute calls _afterCall to finalize the operation state after execution.
executeBatch recomputes the batch id with hashOperationBatch.
executeBatch runs the _beforeCall readiness and predecessor checks once for the batch.
executeBatch loops and performs one external call per array element via _call.
executeBatch calls _afterCall to mark the batch as done after all calls.
_call reaches the arbitrary low-level external call, the primary reentrancy sink of the contract.
Control returns from the untrusted external call to execute/executeBatch and then to _afterCall, so a malicious callee can reenter the timelock while the operation is not yet marked done.
The untrusted callee can re-enter execute (or executeBatch) before _afterCall sets _DONE_TIMESTAMP, potentially replaying a ready operation.
_beforeCall requires isOperationReady(id) before allowing execution.
_beforeCall verifies predecessor completion through isOperationDone, which reads getTimestamp.
_afterCall re-checks isOperationReady(id) before finalizing the operation state.
grantRole is gated by onlyRole(getRoleAdmin(role)), which invokes _checkRole on the caller.
revokeRole is gated by onlyRole(getRoleAdmin(role)), which invokes _checkRole on the caller.
grantRole delegates the actual membership write to _grantRole.
revokeRole delegates the actual membership write to _revokeRole.
renounceRole delegates the membership removal to _revokeRole.
_setupRole grants a role with no caller authorization, so it must only be reachable from a constructor.
The TimelockController constructor configures the admin role relationships via _setRoleAdmin.
The TimelockController constructor bootstraps TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE, PROPOSER_ROLE and EXECUTOR_ROLE through _setupRole.
The TimelockController constructor writes the initial value of _minDelay.
The constructor constants are derived with keccak256 role hashes, mirroring the hashing role of hashOperation.
The Timelock constructor revokes the deployer's admin role via _revokeRole.
The Timelock constructor grants TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE to the configured admin via _setupRole.
The Timelock constructor invokes the TimelockController constructor with delay 6545 and empty proposer/executor arrays.
updateDelay overwrites the stored _minDelay after the self-call check.
hasRole reads the membership flag from the _roles mapping.
_grantRole sets _roles[role].members[account] = true, mutating the authorization state.
_revokeRole sets _roles[role].members[account] = false, mutating the authorization state.
_setRoleAdmin writes _roles[role].adminRole, redefining who may grant/revoke a role.
_checkRole reverts unless hasRole(role, account) is true, enforcing the access-control predicate.
isOperationReady obtains the stored readiness timestamp through getTimestamp.
getTimestamp reads the operation's entry from the _timestamps mapping.
getMinDelay returns the current value of _minDelay.
The caller-supplied target parameter controls which contract execute will call, so it must be bounded by the timelock's authorization flow.
The value parameter determines how much ETH execute forwards in the low-level call.
The arbitrary calldata parameter reaches the low-level external call in _call, enabling reentrant callbacks into the timelock.
The delay parameter is added to block.timestamp by _schedule to compute the readiness time.
newDelay is written into _minDelay by updateDelay, directly changing the protocol's security delay.
The admin address parameter becomes the holder of TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE, a fully privileged role.
The role parameter selects which role's admin is consulted by the onlyRole modifier on grantRole.
The account parameter is compared with _msgSender() in renounceRole to keep self-revocation only.
The minDelay parameter of the TimelockController constructor initializes _minDelay.
The locally computed operation id keys the readiness checks and the state finalization in execute.
The loop index controls iteration over targets/values/datas in executeBatch and the batch schedulers.
The local timestamp read from storage is compared against block.timestamp to decide whether an operation is ready.

normalization_plan.reason: The target parameter has no meaning outside execute and must be normalized into the execute function node that forwards it to the low-level call.
The value parameter exists only to parametrize execute's payable forwarded call and should fold into the execute function node.
The calldata parameter flows directly into the arbitrary external call in _call and should merge into that unsafe-call-bearing function node.
The delay parameter of schedule is only used to derive the stored timestamp and normalizes into the schedule function node.
newDelay is the single mutable input of updateDelay and normalizes into that privileged state-changing function.
The admin argument is consumed only by the Timelock constructor when granting the privileged admin role.
The role identifier is shared plumbing across AccessControl and is anchored to the grantRole entry point for normalization.
The account parameter is compared against the caller in renounceRole, the strictest authorization check on the argument.
minDelay is consumed only by the TimelockController constructor to initialize _minDelay.
The locally computed operation id is produced inside execute/schedule and keys the timelock's readiness checks, so it folds into execute.
The loop counter only exists to iterate the batch arrays in executeBatch and normalizes into that function node.
The local timestamp is read from storage and compared with block.timestamp inside isOperationReady, so it merges into that readiness check.
